adapters.automaticInvocation: requires an external API/agent runner or a user-triggered ChatGPT turn

$comment: PL-AI-0003, the OPTIONAL autonomous dispatcher. Read by scripts/cloud/agent-dispatcher.mjs;
validated by scripts/cloud/dispatch-policy.mjs -> resolveDispatcherConfig.
IT IS OFF, AND TWO SWITCHES MUST BOTH BE ON. `enabled` below is committed state: the
repository has decided this mechanism may exist. `enableEnvVar` is runtime state: this
invocation, on this machine, was armed by whoever started it. Requiring both means a merged
configuration change cannot by itself make a scheduled job start spending money, and an armed
environment cannot dispatch in a checkout that never opted in.
WITH THE VALUES AS SHIPPED, EVERY DISPATCH REFUSES. A candidate collects three refusal codes
at once -- dispatcher_disabled, runner_unavailable and cost_unknown -- and two further
grounds sit behind them, each of which would refuse on its own if the first three were
removed: the budget ceilings are zero, and no human approval record exists. That redundancy
is deliberate. A single switch is a single mistake.
The escalation categories that require a human are NOT restated here. They are read from
control/policies.json -> escalation.humanOnly, because two copies of an escalation policy is
one copy that quietly stops matching.
A ceiling of 0 means NO SPEND HAS BEEN AUTHORIZED, and is refused as such rather than
treated as unlimited. Raising either ceiling is a Budget escalation under
control/policies.json and additionally requires a committed human approval record; the
dispatcher cannot write one, by construction.
The ledger is the durable record of what has already been charged. An ABSENT ledger means
nothing has been spent, which is correct on day one. An UNREADABLE ledger means spend is
unknown, and unknown spend refuses -- otherwise corrupting one file would be how the
budget gets reset.
Attempts are counted from the audit log, so the ceiling survives a process restart. The
backoff is deterministic and unjittered: this is a cross-run attempt budget, not the
within-run smoothing gpt-review-worker.mjs applies to a single upstream.

providers.notes: The intended API-driven path, and a SEAM: no runner with this id is registered in scripts/cloud/dispatch-runners.mjs, so every dispatch through it refuses with runner_unavailable. That is on purpose and is stated rather than hidden -- a model-calling runner cannot be written honestly without a key to exercise it, and this repository already has exactly one audited OpenAI caller (scripts/cloud/gpt-review-worker.mjs). `cost: null` means no cost model has been established, which refuses independently with cost_unknown; a rate table goes here when one is agreed.

The working, credential-free path: it publishes a task_instruction on the agent bus, which is how the shared-repository lane is reached today. Informational by design -- it changes no task state, and the receiving lane still claims and gates its own work. Routed to nothing as shipped; to use it, move "gpt-architect" out of the entry above and into this agentIds list. Its runner declares zeroCost, so it is priced at 0 with basis no_metered_call and needs no budget ceiling and no Budget approval; declaring a cost model here as well would be a contradiction and is refused.
